data.title: Raffles Interior Probe Flags Feasibility Risks in Major Asset Deal
data.description:
Raffles Interior Ltd. ( (HK:1376) ) has issued an announcement.

Raffles Interior Limited announced that independent investigator Kroll (HK) Limited has completed a forensic review into matters surrounding a proposed acquisition of a redevelopment asset, issuing a final report that broadly confirms earlier findings. The investigation highlights that valuation assumptions for the Target Asset relied on a hypothetical redevelopment lacking finalized planning approval, with authorities previously declining a proposal and no substantive evidence of the group or related parties having the resources or capability to undertake a project of the estimated scale.

The report further concludes that, based on the group’s cash balance of about SGD6.2 million at end-2025 and a swing from operating cash inflows in 2023 to outflows in 2025, Raffles Interior would likely have been unable to fund the acquisition consideration and associated development costs without substantial external financing. Trading in the company’s shares remains suspended, underscoring ongoing regulatory and investor scrutiny of its financial capacity and governance around major transactions.

data.title: Prosus Continues Share Buy-Back with €63.8 Million Repurchase
data.description:

Prosus has provided an update on its open-ended share repurchase programme targeting ordinary shares in both Prosus and its parent Naspers, acquired from free-float shareholders. The initiative, first announced in June 2022, is part of a broader capital allocation strategy designed to manage the group’s equity structure and potentially enhance shareholder value.

Between 7 and 11 September 2026, the company bought back 1,771,604 Prosus shares at an average price of €35.99, for a total outlay of about €63.8 million, equivalent to roughly US$74.1 million. The continued execution of the programme under European market abuse regulations underscores Prosus’s commitment to disciplined buy-back activity, with implications for share liquidity and the overall ownership mix within the group.

data.description:

ProVen VCT plc and ProVen Growth and Income VCT plc have begun formal talks over a possible merger that would combine the assets and liabilities of the smaller PGI into ProVen via a scheme of reconstruction under the UK Insolvency Act. The boards say the aim is to simplify the structure, deliver cost savings and administrative efficiency, and create a larger vehicle for VCT investors.

If agreed, PGI shareholders would receive new ProVen shares calculated on the trusts’ relative net asset values, with the deal requiring approval from investors in both funds. The current offers for subscription for each VCT are set to close on 30 September 2026, and ProVen is planning a fresh fundraising later this year for the 2026–27 and 2027–28 tax years, signalling an intention to continue growing the merged platform and its appeal to tax-efficient investors.
